pr.title: Invoice search, share link, notes and CSV export
pr.author: Crashtest author agent

issue.title: Invoice search, share link, notes and CSV export
issue.body:
As someone who sends a lot of invoices, I want to find invoices quickly, share one with a client without making them sign up, keep a note on an invoice, and take my list into a spreadsheet, so I spend less time hunting through pages and answering "can you send that again?" emails.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On the invoice list I can search by client name or invoice number. Search combines with the status filter, and both survive paging.
2. Each row of the invoice list also shows how many line items the invoice has.
3. An invoice has a free-text notes field. I can edit it; it shows on the invoice page.
4. I can create a public share link for an invoice. Anyone with the link sees a read-only page of that invoice (client, line items, total, notes) without signing in. I can revoke the link, after which it shows "not found".
5. I can export the invoices I am looking at (current search and filter) as a CSV file.
6. Everything that worked before still works.

intro: This change adds four things to the invoice app: search on the invoice list, a free-text notes field, a public share link that can be revoked, and a CSV export of the current list. Each list row also shows how many line items the invoice has. The database gets two new invoice columns and a per-workspace change counter that the export cache uses.

stops.why: Notes and share links need two new columns on `invoices`. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` does not change a table that already exists, so the code adds missing columns with `ALTER TABLE` each time a database is opened.

blocks.text: An invoice gets two new fields. `notes` is always a string. `share_token` is `null` until a share link is created.
A new database gets both columns from the `CREATE TABLE` statement.

A database made before this change already has an `invoices` table, so the statement above does nothing for it. This list names the columns to add. The indexes that need those columns are kept apart, so they can be created afterwards.

The search query at a later stop is told to use this index.

notes.text: On an old database this creates nothing for `invoices`, because the table is already there.
The change counter and its triggers. They are shown at the CSV export stop.

focus.why: Decides if ALTER TABLE runs on a database that holds data

With an empty `q` this adds nothing to the clause.
This helper is used by the searched list at the next stop.

blocks.text: `listInvoices` now has two paths. Without search text it runs `browseInvoices`, which is the old code written with the shared helpers. With search text it runs `searchInvoices`, shown at the next stop.

The search text is always empty on this path.

questions.prompt: A user searches for `50%`. Which pattern does `likePattern` return?

questions.prompt: How does a list row get its `line_count`?
options: From a COUNT subquery on line_items, run per invoice
From a counter column stored on the invoice

stops.title: A search reads all matching ids once, then counts and pages in memory
stops.why: During a search the tab counts must follow the search. The code reads every matching invoice once from an index, counts the tabs in JavaScript, and loads full rows only for the page that is shown.

blocks.text: The function starts with two queries. The first finds clients of this workspace whose name matches. The second finds every invoice of this workspace that matches by number or belongs to one of those clients. **It reads only id, status and due date.**

notes.text: `INDEXED BY` makes SQLite use the index created in `LATE_INDEXES`.
The client ids travel as one JSON array, and `json_each` turns it back into rows.

Limits matching invoices to the caller's workspace

blocks.text: Next the tab counts are made from that list, and the page is cut out of it. Look at what `counts.all` is, and at what happens when no id is left for the page.

Full rows, with total and line count, are loaded only for this page's ids.

blocks.text: The `version` comes from the database. This code creates nine triggers: one for each of insert, update and delete on `invoices`, `clients` and `line_items`. Each trigger adds one to the counter of the workspace.

questions.prompt: An invoice's notes are `-5, thanks`. Which text does `csvField` return?
options: -5, thanks
'-5, thanks
"-5, thanks"
"'-5, thanks"
questions.explain: Line 11 puts an apostrophe in front because the text starts with `-`. Line 12 then wraps the result in double quotes because it holds a comma.

questions.prompt: A user downloads an export, marks an invoice paid, and downloads the same export again on the same day. What does the second call to `exportCsv` do?
options: Returns the stored file, because the key is equal
Builds a new file, because the stored version differs
Returns the stored file until the server restarts
Builds a new file, because an entry is used only once
questions.explain: The update fires a trigger that raises the workspace counter. Line 149 uses a stored file only when its `version` equals the current one, so the file is built again.

stops.title: Tests cover each feature through HTTP, but not the export cache
stops.why: The new test file has one group for each feature and one for the schema upgrade. The gaps show the reader what still has to be checked by hand.

blocks.text: The tests sign in as two users from two workspaces and send requests to the app. The search tests check matching, tab counts, paging and escaping. This part sends LIKE wildcards and HTML as search text.
Notes: this test sends two API updates, one without the `notes` key and one with it.
Share links: other tests cover create, public view and revoke. These three check a repeated create, the CSRF token and session, and a user from another workspace.
CSV: this test writes formula text into a client name and into notes, then reads the export.
Schema upgrade: the test builds an old `invoices` table by hand and opens the file with `openDb`.

notes.text: A second open checks that the upgrade can run again without an error.

blocks.text: **Not tested in this file:** no test downloads the same export twice, so the reuse of a stored file and its rebuild after a write are never checked. There is also no test for the Copy button script, for the length limits of search text and notes, or for the Overdue tab count during a search.
